title: Paloma and the Asset
premise: Emrys Iversen, a grief-hollowed air crash investigator, receives a calendar invite from a handler who died in the same wreck that killed his family—row twelve. The invitation pulls him into a buried conspiracy: the crash was engineered to silence a whistleblower, and Emrys's own investigation was steered from the start. Hunted by an assassin who was once the dead handler's lover, and shadowed by a foreign intelligence officer whose loyalties keep shifting, Emrys must decide whether exposing the truth is worth becoming the next name on the list. In the end, he trades his anonymity—and nearly his life—to force the truth into daylight, discovering that the assassin's loyalty, not any government's, is what saves him.
about_author: O. M. Reyes is a former aviation safety analyst who left the field after a decade of reading black-box transcripts no one else wanted to finish. They write thrillers from a coastal town where fog rolls in early and stays late.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Two years after losing his wife and daughter in Flight 4471, Emrys works nights cataloging wreckage photos he can't stop studying. A calendar notification pings: a meeting tomorrow with Dana Whitlock—the intelligence handler listed among the dead in row twelve. The beat: dread sharpened by a terrible flicker of hope.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Emrys verifies the invite's metadata: sent from Whitlock's account, timestamped after her death. He tells no one, breaks protocol, and goes to the meeting point—a shuttered flight museum. He finds her dead drop unlocked and a burner phone waiting. Beat: the investigator becomes the investigated.

chapters.title: Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The phone holds one video: Whitlock, recorded before the crash, confessing that Flight 4471 was downed to bury a passenger—a defector carrying proof of a tri-government arms program. She names Emrys as the only investigator clean enough to trust. Beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: The Cleaner
chapters.summary: Vesper Kane's POV. Vesper, the assassin assigned to erase Whitlock's loose ends, arrives at the museum minutes too late and reads Emrys's presence in the dust. Her employer wants the file destroyed; her own history with Whitlock makes her hesitate for the first time. Beat: a professional's first crack.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Emrys realizes he's being followed through Reykjavik's harbor district and uses his knowledge of cargo routes to slip away, stashing a copy of Whitlock's evidence with a retired colleague, Halvard. Beat: paranoia as a survival skill finally paying off.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. He attempts to hand the file to his own agency and watches it vanish into a review that will take months—or forever. Simultaneously, British and American contacts quietly open files on him. Beat: the institutions he trusted become the threat.

chapters.title: The Woman on the Bridge
chapters.summary: Vesper corners Emrys on a pedestrian bridge but doesn't kill him; instead she asks what Whitlock left behind. Their uneasy bargain forms: she'll verify the file's authenticity before deciding which side of history she's on. Beat: enemies negotiating in the space between duty and doubt.

chapters.title: Black Box
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Re-examining the flight data with fresh eyes, Emrys finds the transponder anomaly he was ordered to ignore two years ago—proof the crash was commanded, not accidental. Someone ransacks his apartment while he's out. Beat: vindication laced with violation.

chapters.title: Halvard's Price
chapters.summary: Halvard agrees to authenticate the evidence but demands Emrys walk away afterward—for his own safety. Before the analysis finishes, Halvard's workshop burns. Emrys pulls him from the smoke; the file survives. Beat: loyalty tested by fire, literally.

chapters.title: Handler Ghost
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper traces who sent her original contract and finds her own agency scrubbed Whitlock's death before it happened—meaning her employers planned the crash. Flashbacks reveal her love for Whitlock and the night she chose the job over the woman. Beat: guilt catching up at speed.

chapters.title: The Defector's Daughter
chapters.summary: Emrys locates the defector's daughter, Lena, living under a new identity. She carries the second half of the proof—a decryption key—and has been running for two years. She trusts no one, least of all a man connected to the original investigation. Beat: two orphans of the same lie.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Emrys, Vesper, and Lena hole up in a coastal safehouse, counting their options: three governments want this buried, one assassin network wants them dead, and the press can't be trusted unvetted. Vesper and Emrys circle each other warily. Beat: exhausted intimacy forming under pressure.

chapters.title: Betrayal Math
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper secretly alerts her old contact to flush out the conspiracy's architect—but the reply reveals her message was anticipated, meaning there's a leak inside their triangle. She conceals this from Emrys. Beat: protection curdling into deception.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: A government strike team hits the safehouse. Emrys and Lena escape through sea caves while Vesper stays behind to cover them—and is captured. Emrys must choose between the mission and going back. Beat: love against duty, made literal.

chapters.title: What Vesper Knows
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Interrogating his own choices, Emrys decodes Whitlock's final message layer: she predicted Vesper would be sent, and asked Emrys to save her if he could. He turns back toward the city with a plan instead of a weapon. Beat: obedience to the dead over fear for the living.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Emrys offers the decryption key to the conspiracy's architect, Undersecretary Corliss, in exchange for Vesper—while feeding the real key's location to a journalist he's spent chapters vetting. Beat: the quiet man bluffing a state.

chapters.title: Corliss
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Face to face with Corliss, Vesper learns the full scope: the arms program, the crash, and the plan to pin everything on Emrys as a rogue investigator. She plays along until the extraction window opens. Beat: the assassin choosing a side.

chapters.title: Ninety Seconds
chapters.summary: The escape goes wrong; Corliss's men corner them on the tarmac of a private airfield. Vesper takes a bullet shielding Emrys; Emrys broadcasts the decrypted files to every newsroom and embassy he can reach before the signal dies. Beat: climax—truth released at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The publication detonates across three governments; inquiries open, Corliss is arrested, and Emrys is both celebrated and disowned by his former agency. Vesper survives surgery but faces charges. Beat: hollow victory, honestly rendered.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Emrys testifies publicly, naming row twelve and every passenger—including his family—as victims of a decision made in a conference room. Vesper, granted limited immunity for her testimony, corroborates everything. Beat: grief given a public shape at last.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Months later, Emrys visits the graves and, for the first time since the crash, sleeps through the night. Vesper, released under supervision, appears at his door—not forgiven, but present. Beat: the possibility of peace without forgetting.

chapters.title: Flight Path
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, closing frame. He takes a commercial flight—his first since the crash—and watches the rows fill with strangers living ordinary lives. A letter from Whitlock's estate arrives: she'd trusted him because he never stopped asking why. Final beat: identity rebuilt around truth rather than loss.
